The mean identity mʹ=fδ(m)+[(3m−9/10)/4]V−P/2 is exact; as heterogeneity decays, strict monotonicity of the scalar fδ with three isolated fixed points proves convergence. The intermediate uniform equilibrium has hyperbolic eigenvalues λ>1 and ℓ∈(0,1); stable-manifold invariance gives a=k/(ℓ²−λ) and at δ=7/25 c=1/[2(λ−ℓ³)]=32000000/46977489. Cooperative ordering and the stable manifold separate extinction from endemicity. Independent SymPy coefficient identities reproduced all pair differences and cubic constant; finite trajectory diagnostics do not prove all-small-t limits.

final_claim: For the explicit deterministic three-agent pairwise-plus-triangle SIS Euler mean-field map and recovery 1/10<δ<121/400, every cube orbit converges to a uniform equilibrium 0,p_- or p_+. The local saddle basin boundary has quadratic coefficient a=k(p_-)/(ℓ²−λ), which changes sign uniquely at δ=7/25. At that value it instead has cubic coefficient 32000000/46977489 multiplying centered P=y1y2y3, so two small positive infection profiles with identical mean 3/10 and variance 2t² but opposite centered third products converge to extinction and endemic (3/5,3/5,3/5), respectively.
limitations: Map parameters: h=1/2, pairwise 1/20 per neighbor, triangle coefficient one, 1/10<δ<121/400.
The global convergence theorem concerns the exact deterministic map and relies on strict contraction, not finite simulation.
